segments.oily: One reviewer with acne-prone oily skin reports the cream caused a severe breakout across her face, neck and chest, while other reviewers with oily skin report no breakouts or irritation and a matte, non-shiny finish.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin, including some with eczema or facing winter dryness, consistently report strong, long-lasting hydration and relief from tight or flaky patches.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin, including one in a desert climate, report the cream moisturizes dry or flaky patches well without leaving skin oily.
segments.sensitive: Most reviewers with sensitive skin, including several managing psoriasis, rosacea or a tretinoin burn, report no burning, stinging or irritation, but one reviewer who broke out badly warns that sensitive or acne-prone skin should be cautious with this formula's cetyl alcohol content.
segments.normal: One reviewer with normal skin says they only reach for this heavier cream during the dry winter months, using a lighter lotion the rest of the year.
segments.mature: Reviewers with mature skin, including several in their 50s, 60s and 70s, report firmer, smoother, less crepey-looking skin and reduced dryness, though one 77-year-old cautions that no cream reverses deeper wrinkles or lost collagen.

concerns.aging: Many reviewers report smoother, plumper skin and less noticeable fine lines within weeks, but a couple caution it will not reverse deeper wrinkles or sagging — it moisturizes rather than delivering a dramatic anti-aging transformation.
concerns.dehydration: Deep, long-lasting hydration is the most frequently reported benefit, with reviewers describing soft, plump skin that is still hydrated the next morning, even for very dry skin.
concerns.redness: Reviewers report reduced redness and calmer-looking skin by morning, including some managing rosacea alongside other treatments, with no reviewer reporting new redness caused by the cream.
concerns.barrier: Several reviewers, including ones managing psoriasis or retinol-related irritation, say the cream feels like it strengthens or repairs their skin barrier and leaves skin balanced rather than dry or overloaded.
concerns.spots: A few reviewers report faded acne scars or discoloration and a more even-looking skin tone after a few weeks of use.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers, including several with oily or acne-prone skin, report no clogged pores or breakouts, but a few describe new breakouts, including one reviewer whose face, neck and chest broke out badly and who warns sensitive or acne-prone skin to be cautious.
concerns.oiliness: Most reviewers describe the cream absorbing to a matte, non-greasy finish despite its rich texture, though one reviewer noted it felt a bit oily on the skin right after applying.

extraits.titre: Made Me Break Out All Over
extraits.texte: I'm in my mid-20s and have started taking my skin care routine more seriously, to avoid premature aging as I get older. I've always had very acne-prone, oily skin; I tried everything under the sun as a teenager up until my only other option was Accutane, which my mother thankfully wouldn't allow me to go on. Now that I'm older I still have the occasional pimple, but nothing terrible since I use a salicylic acid cleanser every morning. I also started using Niacinamide, which made my face even less red and acne non-existent for the past month! However, I also started using a retinol cream which dried out my skin a bit, so I tried this night cream because it had just great reviews, is labeled non-comedogenic, etc. My acne is now as bad as it was when I was in middle school! I'm broke out across my chin, the bridge of my nose, neck, and chest. I haven't had acne on my neck or chest since puberty. If I had used it longer it might've moisturized my skin, and the scent isn't bad. But if you have sensitive or acne-prone skin, just be careful. This had cetyl alcohol in it (which is what makes it so thick and creamy). Normally this isn't a bad thing, but I've now read this can cause sensitive skin to break out. Apparently it's best to stick to thin or light moisturizers if you have these skin conditions, which I'm definitely now doing!

extraits.titre: It's time for CeraVe to solve this unsanitary packaging issue!
extraits.texte: Adding to my review below... I have now switched to CeraVe PM Facial Moisturing Lotion, which comes well-packaged in a pump bottle. See photo of ingredients for comparison with the Renewing Night Cream. The main difference is Shea Butter. I live in a humid climate and have normal skin, so I don't need a heavier moisturizer until the short, dry winter season. For now, I am very happy with the "PM" lotion. I received my 5th jar of Renewing Night Cream, but sadly had to return it due to sloppy, careless packaging on the part of CeraVe (not Amazon's mailer). The CeraVe box was dented, but worst of all, the lid wasn't screwed onto the jar! It was loosely sitting on top. The cream looked odd, like it had been exposed to air (and who knows what else). CeraVe has never bothered to put a seal under the lid, nor shrinkwrap around the box - either of which would solve this ongoing problem. I kept reordering it because I like the results - it's a very good skincare product - while hoping that they would improve the packaging. But this time I didn't even want to put the cream on my face. I have 4 other types of CeraVe lotions that are safely packaged - it's a great, affordable brand. I would pay a dollar more for this Night Cream if it came in a sealed jar.

This moisturizer ticks all the boxes. No scent that I can tell, very moisturizing for my sensitive combination skin that gets dry and flakey in spots ( i am 26 years old) I have only been using a week, so haven't noticed much of a difference besides moisturizing when I apply it. My issue here is the amount. I saw tons of reviews from customers with half full containers and I thought “It can’t be all of them!” Sure enough mine came in the mail literally half empty. It was a good price but for half the amount I do not think I will purchase again.

extraits.titre: A Simple, Affordable Night Cream That Actually Works
extraits.texte: Let me just say this upfront: you do not need a $98 cream in a fancy jar to have soft, glowing, younger-looking skin. I’m 54, my skin is dry, and I get asked if I’m in my 30s on the regular. This CeraVe Night Cream is a big part of why. I know it’s technically marketed for nighttime, but my skin is Sahara-level dry, so I use it during the day too. I layer a tiny bit of castor oil underneath (an aesthetician recommended that combo to me), and my face stays moisturized, calm, and honestly as soft as a baby’s bottom. What I Love: • Deep hydration without feeling greasy It’s thick in the jar but melts right into your skin — perfect under makeup or on its own. • Gentle, no-fragrance formula My skin is sensitive, and this doesn’t irritate or break me out at all. • Peptides + ceramides + hyaluronic acid Basically all the things every expensive brand brags about… except this one is actually affordable. • Skin looks smoother and more rested After a few weeks, my fine lines looked less noticeable and my skin barrier felt stronger. A quick heads up: It doesn’t come with an inner seal inside the jar — that’s normal for this product, but good to mention for anyone wondering. Bottom Line: This is one of the best moisturizers you can buy at this price point. If you have dry or mature skin, skip the pricey stuff and try this first. Your skin (and your wallet) will thank you.

extraits.titre: An Affordable Night Cream That Actually Holds Its Own on Mature, Dry Skin
extraits.texte: I’m 52 with post-menopausal, mature dry skin, and I don’t keep products around that don’t genuinely perform. I use everything from high-end Korean and medical-grade skincare to very simple drugstore staples — and this night cream has earned its place. The texture is richer than it looks but never heavy or greasy. It spreads easily, sinks in well, and immediately makes my skin feel comfortable and supported rather than coated. By morning, my skin looks smoother, calmer, and more rested, with noticeably less dryness and that tight, crepey feeling that can show up overnight with mature skin. What stands out most is how well this works as a recovery cream. When my skin is feeling overworked from actives, dehydrated, or just off, this consistently helps bring it back into balance. It layers beautifully over serums without pilling, seals everything in, and doesn’t irritate — even on nights when my skin is more sensitive than usual. Despite the affordable price, this doesn’t feel basic or flimsy. The hydration lasts, my skin barrier feels stronger over time, and I wake up with skin that looks healthier, not just temporarily moisturized. It’s fragrance-free, reliable, and quietly effective — exactly what a night cream should be. This may not be flashy or trendy, but if you have dry, mature, or easily dehydrated skin and want something that simply works night after night, this is a very smart choice. I’m 56, very fair with freckles and ultra sensitive skin. I started using Tretinoin and burnt my skin. After watching tutorials, I armed myself with CeraVe products and this night cream is heavenly. First, the box arrived undamaged and as you can see the cream is full and untouched. This cream is dense and has a luxurious feel as you apply. There’s no burning sensation and my skin looks quite dewy/moisturized. I also use CeraVe skin repair ointment for the severe burn areas. Gone is the Tret “purge” with all the peeling and irritation. Now I have the full AM/PM routine anchored with CeraVe products that are recommended by my dermatologist. The price point is fantastic compared to the department store prices and the results are one happy complexion. I will restart Tret now that I am prepared for any bad reaction because the CeraVe line works perfectly with my difficult, sun damaged and sensitive skin. Thank you CeraVe!

The container is very small so I was skeptical for the price but a little goes a long way since the consistency is very thick but not oily. I have super oily skin and this doesn’t cause any break outs or irritation and I use it at night with my differin cream.
